IS 13485 ( Part 1 ) : 1992 

(Reaffirmed 1997) 



Indian Standard 

FORESTRY TOOLS — STALK PULLER 

SPECIFICATION 

PART 1 LIGHT DUTY 



UDC 630-3 



© BIS 1992 

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 

July 1992 Price Grou P 2 



Forestry and Plantation Crops Machinery Sectional Committee, FAD 40 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Forestry and Plantation Crops^ Machinery Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 

Removal of stalks by pulling by hand is very difficult and time consuming. For this purpose 
stalk pullers have been developed and are being used. Considering the use of stalk puller for 
pulling out the stalks of lantena species in the forest, a need was felt to prepare this standard 
for helping in quality production of this tool. 

The Part 2 of this standard which is under preparation would specify the requirements for the 
stalk puller, heavy duty which are used for pulling out the stalks of species other than lantena 
species in the forest. 

In the preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from the Forest Operations 
Division, Forest Research Institute ( ICFRE ), Dehra Dun. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : I960 * Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )\ 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard. 



IS 13485 ( Part 1 ) : 1992 



Indian Standard 



FORESTRY TOOLS — STALK PULLER 

SPECIFICATION 



PART 1 LIGHT DUTY 



1 SCOPE 

This standard ( Part 1 ) specifies the materials, 
dimensions and other requirements for stalk 
puller, light duty used for uprooting bushes 
such as lantena, etc. 

2 REFERENCES 

The Indian Standards which are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard is given in Annex A. 

3 MATERIALS 

Various component of stalk pullers shall be 
made from the materials given below : 



Component 
Tongue 

Other components 
( stay, handles, and 
supports ) 

Wheel 

Knurling plate 

Stay 



Material 

Mild steel 

(see IS 226 : 1975) 

Mild steel 

(see IS 226 : 1975) 

Hard Rubber ( Solid ) 

High carbon steel 
(see IS 2507 : 1975 ) 

Heavy duty conduit 
pipe 



4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

The dimensions of light duty stalk pullers shall 
be as given in Fig. 1 

4.1 The tolerances for various dimensions 
shall be of coarse class specified in IS 2102 
( Part 1 ) : 1980. 

5 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

5*1 Knurling shall be provided on tongue and 
stay as shown in Fig. 1 so that there is proper 
holding of bushes. 

5.2 Wheels shall be free and stalk puller shall 
move on these wheels smoothly* 

5.3 The fulcrum shall be free from any play. 



5.4 The notch in the jaws shall be properly 
formed. 

6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 The entire surface of the puller except the 
jaw shall be smooth. 

6*2 The stalk puller shall be free from defects 
such as cracks, rust, burrs and other manufac- 
turing defects. 

6.3 All sharp corners shall be rounded off. 

6.4 The steel pipe, if used, shall be galvanized 
or painted with rust preventive coatings. Other 
steel components shall be painted with rust 
preventive coatings. 

6.5 The welding shall not be porous. 

7 PERFORMANCE TEST 

7.1 An assembled puller shall be placed on a 
horizontal surface and operated for at least 25 
times, to observe the smooth opening and 
closing of the jaws. 

8 DESIGNATION 

The designation shall include the type of the 
stalk puller and the number of this Indian 
Standard as: 

Stalk puller, Light Duty, IS 13485 ( Part 1 ). 

9 MARKING 

9,1 Each stalk puller shall be marked as 
follows: 

a) Manufacturer's name or registered trade- 
mark; 

b) Model number; 

c) Batch, code, or serial number; and 

d) Type. 

9.1.1 Standard Marking 

Each stalk puller may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 



IS 13485 ( Part 1 ) : 1992 



10 PACKING 

The stalk pullers shall be suitably packed to 
avoid damage in handling and transit. 

11 SAMPLING 

In order to ascertain the conformity of the lot, 
the procedure for sampling inspection as given 
in IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1983 shall be followed. 
The inspection level and AQL for various 



characteristics 
and 11.2. 



shall be according to 11.1 



11.1 For dimensions, workmanship and finish, 
a single sampling plan with inspection level IV 
and AQL of 4 percent given in Tables 1 and 2 
of IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1983 shall be followed. 

11-2 For hardness and other requirements a 
single sampling plan with inspection level 11 
and AQL of 4 percent as given in Tables 1 and 2 
of IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1983 shall be followed.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark 
on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system 
of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and 
operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by 
BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard- Details of conditions under 
which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standard 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designation. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
( Publications ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if 
any, are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in 
possession of the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard maybe 
sent to BIS giving the following reference:
